title: PERC rule
subtitle: PE rule-out in selected very-low-risk adults
summary: PERC is used only after pulmonary embolism has already been judged clinically very unlikely and a credible alternative diagnosis is more likely.
population: Clinically stable adults aged 18 years or over in an appropriate acute-care setting when PE suspicion is low on overall clinical assessment and another diagnosis is feasible.
exclusions: Do not use in children, pregnancy or puerperium, haemodynamic instability or severe illness, suspected PE during therapeutic anticoagulation, or as a standalone prehospital discharge rule.
NICE notes that PERC has not been validated in people with COVID-19.

criteria.label: PE suspicion is low on overall clinical assessment
criteria.description: Estimated pre-test probability below about 15%, with no unresolved features making PE a realistic diagnosis.

criteria.label: Another diagnosis is feasible
criteria.description: For example chest-wall pain reproduced by focal palpation or movement, without unexplained dyspnoea, syncope, hypoxia or unilateral leg findings.

criteria.label: Oxygen saturation below 95% on room air
criteria.description: An oxygen-supported or unobtainable room-air measurement cannot satisfy PERC rule-out. Do not remove clinically required oxygen to obtain a value.

criteria.label: Surgery or trauma within the previous 4 weeks requiring hospitalisation

results.label: PERC not yet applicable
interpretation: Confirm that PE is already clinically very unlikely and that a credible alternative diagnosis is more likely.
actions: If PE remains suspected and PERC eligibility is absent or uncertain, follow the suspected PE pathway

results.label: PERC negative
interpretation: Within a correctly selected low-risk population, PE is sufficiently unlikely that further PE testing is generally not required. PE is not impossible, and overall disposition must consider other diagnoses.
actions: Document eligibility and all 8 negative criteria; further PE testing is generally not needed
Base disposition on the complete assessment and other diagnoses; provide safety-net advice if discharged

results.label: PERC positive
interpretation: PE cannot be ruled out using PERC. This does not diagnose PE; continue through the appropriate PE assessment pathway.
actions: PERC cannot exclude PE. If PE remains suspected, use the 2-level PE Wells pathway
Wells 4 or less leads to D-dimer; Wells above 4 leads to immediate imaging. Follow the receiving pathway for delays, interim anticoagulation and disposition

overrides: PERC is used only after low clinical suspicion is established; do not infer eligibility from a Wells score.
A positive PERC result does not diagnose PE and does not itself indicate imaging, admission or anticoagulation.
limitations: Eligibility is a prerequisite and is not part of the numerical score.
All eight PERC criteria must be negative for a negative result.
